focus: Anatomy of the measured verdict: corpus geometry, baseline blindness, label composition

title: The labeled corpus is 100% cross-body; the near-line class has zero pairs in the tracked corpus.
The merge baseline answers different on all 124 classed pairs under both dedup settings, so B=12 is the constant-different score on the 12 different labels.
The 48 same / 12 different label split sets the W=44/L=3 asymmetry arithmetically.
The printed p is the exact binomial tail for 44 of 47 disagreements: 17344/2^47 = 1.2324e-10.
Jev scores sensitivity 44/48, specificity 9/12, precision 44/47; the four same misses sit just under 0.5 and the three different misses are confident false-merges at 0.68-0.93.
The AB repeat in the AB/BA/AB order breaks 1-1 ties toward AB and caused two of the four same-labeled misses.
F=3 of 180 calls: 57 pairs answered 3-0 and 3 answered 2-1, so the errors are not sampling noise.
The measured run cost 181 calls, 11752 estimated input tokens and 58.2 s summed call wall for 60 pairs; the census is zero-call and reproducible.

direction: The verdict demonstrates the merge's near-line collapse rule was defeated on its own class
